items.q: The adenoma carcinoma sequence begins most characteristically with loss of which gene?
items.exp: APC loss activates Wnt signalling initiating adenomas; KRAS mutation grows them and TP53 loss completes malignant transformation over years. Germline APC causes familial polyposis.
r: Incorrect. TP53 loss is a late completing step.
Correct. APC loss initiates adenomas.
Incorrect. KRAS acts after initiation in growth.
Incorrect. MLH1 germline defines Lynch pathway instead.
items.kp: Sequence memory: APC first, KRAS middle, TP53 last.

items.q: Hundreds of colonic adenomas by age 16 with certain cancer without surgery indicate which syndrome?
items.exp: FAP from germline APC produces hundreds to thousands of adenomas in adolescence with inevitable cancer by midlife without prophylactic colectomy, plus duodenal and desmoid risks.
r: Incorrect. Lynch has few polyps with repair deficiency.
Correct. Carpeted polyps in teens mean FAP.
Incorrect. Peutz Jeghers gives hamartomas with lip pigmentation.
Incorrect. Juvenile polyps are hamartomatous in children.
items.kp: Count polyps: hundreds equals FAP, few plus fast equals Lynch.

items.q: Microsatellite instability with loss of MLH1 staining and family endometrial cancers indicate what?
items.exp: Lynch syndrome from germline mismatch repair mutation (MLH1, MSH2 and others) causes microsatellite unstable right sided colon and endometrial cancers with accelerated polyp progression.
r: Incorrect. Attenuated FAP still follows APC polyp burden.
Correct. Repair loss plus family spectrum means Lynch.
Incorrect. MUTYH is recessive polyposis with many adenomas.
Incorrect. Sporadic MSI exists via methylation but family pattern here is Lynch.
items.kp: Repair proteins missing in tumour: test the germline for Lynch.

items.q: Which polyp features carry highest malignant transformation risk?
o: Large villous adenoma over 2 cm with high grade dysplasia
items.exp: Size over 1 to 2 cm, villous architecture and high grade dysplasia multiply cancer risk in adenomas, guiding complete excision and surveillance intervals. Small rectal hyperplastic polyps are innocuous.
r: Incorrect. Small tubular adenomas rarely harbour cancer.
Correct. Large villous high grade adenomas risk most.
Incorrect. Rectal hyperplastic polyps are benign.
Incorrect. Pseudopolyps are inflammatory regeneration, not premalignant.
items.kp: Big, villous and dysplastic: the dangerous adenoma triad.

items.q: Right sided colon cancer most often presents how?
o: Occult bleeding with iron deficiency anaemia and vague right iliac mass
items.exp: Wide right colon with liquid stool lets cancers grow silently bleeding occultly into anaemia, while narrow left colon obstructs early with habit change and visible blood. Rectal cancers cause tenesmus.
r: Incorrect. Obstruction typifies left sided lesions.
Correct. Anaemia and vague mass mark right cancers.
Incorrect. Visible bleeding with tenesmus suggests rectal disease.
Incorrect. Screening finds some but presentation here is anaemia.
items.kp: Unexplained iron deficiency in older adults: scope the right colon.

items.q: CEA (carcinoembryonic antigen) in colorectal cancer is properly used how?
o: Postoperative surveillance for recurrence after curative treatment
items.exp: CEA lacks sensitivity and specificity for screening but rising postoperative levels warn of recurrence, triggering imaging. It also tracks metastatic treatment response.
r: Incorrect. CEA cannot screen due to false results both ways.
Correct. Surveillance and monitoring are its roles.
Incorrect. Polyps need endoscopic detection.
Incorrect. No blood test replaces colonoscopy here.
items.kp: CEA watches treated cancer; it never hunts new cancer.

items.q: Mucocutaneous lip pigmentation with hamartomatous polyps and intussusception indicates which syndrome?
items.exp: Peutz Jeghers (STK11) gives perioral pigmentation and hamartomatous polyps causing intussusception and bleeding, with raised pancreatic and other cancer risks needing surveillance.
r: Incorrect. Gardner adds osteomas to FAP adenomas.
Correct. Pigmented lips plus hamartomas mean Peutz Jeghers.
Incorrect. Cowden gives trichilemmomas and breast thyroid risks (PTEN).
Incorrect. Turcot pairs polyposis with brain tumours.
items.kp: Spotted lips plus intussusception equals Peutz Jeghers.

items.q: Bilateral ovarian metastases from a signet ring colon or gastric cancer are eponymously called what?
items.exp: Krukenberg tumours are metastatic signet ring cell deposits (usually gastric, also colorectal) to both ovaries, mimicking primary ovarian cancer and signalling advanced disease.
r: Correct. Metastatic signet ring ovaries are Krukenberg tumours.
Incorrect. Meigs is fibroma with effusions, benign.
Incorrect. Brenner is a primary transitional ovarian tumour.
Incorrect. Walthard rests are benign tubal inclusions.
items.kp: Signet rings in both ovaries: find the gut primary.

items.q: Streptococcus gallolyticus (bovis) bacteraemia should prompt which investigation?
items.exp: Streptococcus gallolyticus bacteraemia and endocarditis associate strongly with colonic adenomas and cancer, mandating colonoscopy even without bowel symptoms.
r: Incorrect. Echo assesses endocarditis but misses the colonic source clue.
Correct. Scope the colon after this bacteraemia.
Incorrect. Airways are not the associated site.
Incorrect. Marrow does not reveal the association.
items.kp: Bovis in blood means look in the colon.

items.q: Sessile serrated lesions cause cancer mainly through which molecular route?
o: BRAF mutation with CpG methylation silencing repair genes
items.exp: Serrated pathway lesions (right sided, flat) acquire BRAF mutation and widespread methylation (CIMP) silencing MLH1, causing microsatellite unstable cancers distinct from classic adenomas and easily missed endoscopically.
r: Incorrect. APC starts classic adenomas, not serrated lesions.
Correct. BRAF plus methylation drives serrated cancers.
Incorrect. KRAS activates rather than deletes in pathways.
Incorrect. Germline TP53 is Li Fraumeni, not serrated polyps.
items.kp: Flat right sided serrated lesions methylate their way to cancer.
